# Robust Reasoning Processes

> A small textbook for a proposed field: the study and engineering of reasoning processes — peer review, prediction markets, audits, LLM judge pipelines, debate protocols — that deliver trustworthy conclusions at known cost and resist corruption. Maintained by QURI (quantifieduncertainty.org) as part of the CAIRN project. Everything is a dated, versioned working draft; formalisms are graded [exact] / [standard shape] / [heuristic].

Core quantities: epistemic weight (a process's likelihood-ratio profile), cost per validated bit, and the corruption cost curve (minimum adversary spend to distort output by a given amount). The field's central empirical project is replacing qualitative ratings with measurements of these quantities. Sibling wiki: Evaluation Engineering (https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org), on producing evaluations at scale and known cost.


## Start Here

- [1. Robust Reasoning Processes](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/start-here/introduction/): A small textbook for a new field — the study and engineering of reasoning processes that deliver trustworthy conclusions at known cost and resist corruption.
- [2. Cruxes](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/start-here/key-questions/): The central uncertainties this wiki is organized around — the questions whose answers would most change what we work on.

## Part I — The Judge

- [3. The Core Model](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/core-model/): The field's basic quantities — epistemic weight, the loss pipeline, unit economics, the corruption cost curve, and prospective information pricing — each graded by how much to trust it.
- [4. Epistemic Impact Analysis](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/proposals/epistemic-impact-analysis/): A framework for quantifying the value of information by how it improves a calibrated AI agent's beliefs.
- [5. Constructing Utility Functions](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/constructing-utility-functions/): Methods for building the weighted question portfolios that Epistemic Impact Analysis and Overseeing Automated Research treat as utility functions — formats, elicitation, empirical results, and the LLM upgrade.
- [6. Untrustworthy Sources](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/untrustworthy-sources/): Most of the defense against being lied to happens before the liar speaks. A security-games model of strategic information — reduce the attack surface at design-time, then on the few channels that won't close, trust a message only as far as a liar couldn't have cheaply faked it.
- [Interlude: The Funding Effect](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/case-studies/the-funding-effect/): The cleanest measured instance of corruption moving a process's epistemic weight — what learning that research was funded by an interested party does to the likelihood ratio of its conclusions.

## Part II — The Processes

- [7. The Process Catalogue](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/process-catalogue/): Reasoning processes compared on the field's two axes — cost to extract validated information, and cost to corrupt — with scope and built-in biases per process.
- [8. What Grounds an Oversight Protocol?](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/oversight-protocols/): A taxonomy of scalable oversight protocols — debate, market-making, prediction games, consistency — by what their incentives ground out in.
- [9. Consistency Evaluations](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/proposals/consistency-evals/): Evaluating AI estimation agents by whether they can be arbitraged, not just whether they are accurate.
- [10. What Is a Strong Reasoner?](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/what-is-a-strong-reasoner/): A working definition of "strong reasoner" — an AI system whose judgments deserve substantial weight, in the limit deference, within its domain.

## Part III — Hardening

- [11. Hardening: Overview](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/hardening-techniques/): The constructive layer — eliminate confident error, and turn six families of lever (calibration, verifiability asymmetry, independence, invariance, incentive-compatibility, deterrence) using oversight affordances no human consultant would tolerate.
- [12. Calibration](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/hardening-calibration/): Make the output's confidence claims true, so the only unboundedly dangerous state — confident error — becomes rare and priced.
- [13. Verifiability Asymmetry](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/hardening-verifiability/): Make checking cheaper than producing, then spot-check — the engine under SAT, proof-carrying code, and the PCP theorem, ported to estimates.
- [14. Independence & Decorrelation](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/hardening-independence/): Manufacture genuinely independent signals so corruption must defeat all of them and herding cannot collapse them.
- [15. Invariance & Low Sensitivity](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/hardening-invariance/): Make the output a function of truth-relevant variables and near-invariant to whatever an adversary controls; rate processes by their breakdown point.
- [16. Incentive-Compatibility](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/hardening-incentives/): Make honest reporting the agent's best strategy through scoring rules and markets, so distortion costs the producer.
- [17. Deterrence](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/hardening-deterrence/): Off-equilibrium penalties that cost almost nothing on the honest path and a great deal to an adversary — the only family that reaches the empty quadrant.
- 18. Certification and Gyms (planned) — planned, not yet written

## Part IV — The Environment

- [19. Identity & Track Records](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/environment/identity-and-track-records/): The institution every incentive scheme in this book silently assumes — identities that make penalties stick and make "n independent reports" mean n, and track records that cost time to fake — and what changes when the reporters are copyable AI processes.
- 20–22. Markets, Law, Culture (planned) — planned, not yet written

## Part V — Applications

- [23. The Reliability Ladder](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/epistemic-applications/): What strong reasoners could be used for — five application tiers, each requiring more warranted trust than the last.
- [24. Overseeing Automated Research](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/proposals/overseeing-automated-research/): Output-metered oversight — managing research you cannot check, by marking its epistemic impact to market.
- [25. LLM Epistemics in Production](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/case-studies/llm-epistemics-in-production/): QURI's deployed systems — RoastMyPost, Squiggle AI, and an LLM-judged Fermi competition — as small working instances of this wiki's abstractions.
- [26. Open Problems](https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org/open-questions/): The field's unresolved problems, aggregated from every chapter's open-questions section.
